why: Same vocabulary (IsFace/degIndex of LocalModel.toMPolyfold, ScRetraction, IsSubMPolyfold, subPolyfold, IsTame). A ⇒ B: B's retraction s : V* → V* onto F is the S of proposition_2_5_15 (S.U ⊆ R.U, F ⊆ S.U, S.retract = F), after moving F between ↥O and E₀ with isFace_toMPolyfold_iff (V2_46, not banned); B's explicit sub-M-polyfold data for s|_{O∩V*} (sc-smooth in the M-polyfold O, V → V, idempotent, image F ∩ V) is not a theorem of A but the body of the proof of isSubMPolyfold_of_isFace, re-done for an arbitrary retraction onto F (subData_of, ~90 lines of glue copied from the project); the tame/degree clause is isSubMPolyfold_of_isFace + proposition_2_5_15_isTame (proof irrelevance; paracompactness from paracompactSpace_subtype). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: A pins down the construction — S = r ∘ P_i with P_i = killCoord T i and F ⊆ f_i (proposition_2_5_15), a tame model of F through faceProj (proposition_2_5_15_tameModel), the chart-compatibility lemma faceChart_compatible_subChart, the coordinate identity degIndexWith = quadrantDeg ∘ faceProj + 1 and the killCoord lemmas — while B only asserts that some retraction onto F exists plus the conclusions. B does give isSubMPolyfold_of_isFace (B_to_isSubMPolyfold) and proposition_2_5_15_isTame for any sub-M-polyfold proof/instance (B_to_isTame), both rt_check OK. Harness: the statement of proposition_2_5_15_isTame contains the banned isSubMPolyfold_of_isFace (argument of subPolyfold), so any proof mentioning A fails #rt_check and #rt_check_soft (verified); A_to_B := A'_to_B ∘ A_to_A' with A' = A up to that proof term (A_to_A' by proof irrelevance), and #rt_check passes on A'_to_B.
overlap: n/a (B_to_A not proved); the partial results B_to_isSubMPolyfold / B_to_isTame use only B and IsTameWith.isTame.
